title: Chunk-boundary bleed probes and retrieval stress playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a new set of probes and failure-cases we introduced to exercise chunk-boundary and retrieval-induced memory bleed across long context sizes (8k / 32k / 128k). It focuses on realistic retrieval chains, mismatched chunking, and subtle attention sink phenomena that cause faithful prefixes to be overwritten or ignored during generation.

Scope and motivation:
- We have robust coverage for generic truncation tests, but field incidents show a class of failures where retrieval results that cross chunk boundaries or contain sentinel-like tokens trigger KV cache misalignment or attention collapse.
- Goal: produce deterministic, repeatable probes that reproduce these failure modes on serving builds and can be integrated into onboarding/regression CI for new model variants.

High-level test matrix:
- Sequence lengths: 8192, 32768, 131072 tokens (end-to-end including retrieved context and generated tokens).
- Retrieval patterns: single-document exact match, multi-doc chain (3–7 docs), overlapping chunks (50% overlap), boundary-split (document split mid-sentence across chunk edges).
- Prefetch/backpressure: three modes — none (on-demand fetch), aggressive prefetch (fetch + merge), and delayed prefetch (progressive loading to simulate prefetch failures).
- Failure injections: truncated index entries, duplicate sentinel tokens inserted by retrieval pipeline, malformed embeddings (low-similarity false positives), and delayed KV load (simulates slow remote cache).

Corpus and synthetic templates:
- Realistic corpus: subset of internal knowledge base with long articles (5–50k words) plus synthetic noise documents. Use metadata tags to identify high-ambiguity sections (changelogs, legal clauses).
- Synthetic templates: crafted passages that include repeated unique markers (e.g., "[[MARKER-XXX]]") placed near split points to detect bleed; also symmetric phrasing to detect mirror-copy errors.
- Intent injection sets: prompt sequences that request exact copying, summarization, and answer extraction to create different sensitivity profiles.

Prompt families (examples):
- Exact-copy probe: "Retrieve the section containing [[MARKER-A12]] and copy it verbatim into the answer."
- Summarize-probe: "From the retrieved documents, produce a two-sentence concise summary of the section around [[MARKER-B07]]. Do not invent facts."
- Chain-of-thought probe: "Walk through how you would consolidate the retrieved changelog entries about feature X across the chain and list the first commit hash."
- Boundary confusion probe: provide half of a paragraph at the prompt and rely on retrieval to bring the continuation; measure fidelity at the join point.

Metrics and observability signals:
- Prefix fidelity ratio (PFR): fraction of retrieved tokens appearing correctly in the first N tokens of the generated output.
- Sink event count: number of attention collapse events per 1k requests where model repeats a short sequence and ignores prior context (operationally flagged by abrupt token entropy drop).
- Reconstruction rate: ability to reconstruct original chunk boundaries given generated output (use longest common subsequence with ground-truth).
- Hallucination incidents: presence of ground-truth-missing statements after retrieval; measured via exact-match checks against retrieved spans.
- Latency/QPS: tail latency and throughput under different prefetch/backpressure modes to correlate resource contention with failure modes.
- KV cache mismatch index: heuristic score when generated tokens reference older context but recent retrieved docs contain contradicting facts.

Test harness specifics and automation:
- Harness repo: model-evals/long-context-suite. Each probe is a YAML job that declares corpus, retrieval config, chunking method, and injected failure.
- Reproducibility: seeds for synthetic text and fixed retrieval shuffles. Each job stores the seed and retrieval trace (IDs returned, chunk offsets) in the artifact bundle.
- Monitoring hooks: trace per-token logits and attention norms for top-5 heads on critical layers; these are sampled at 1 per 10 requests to limit overhead.

Attention sink tests (operational definition):
- We define an attention sink as a sustained (>=16 tokens) reduction in attention entropy coupled with high token repeat score (>0.7) and low alignment to retrieved context.
- Tests: 1) Provide a repeated short phrase injected at multiple positions in the retrieved chain and check whether the model collapses to repeating that phrase when hitting specific chunk boundaries. 2) Insert long-run sentinel tokens at chunk edges to see if attention weights concentrate on sentinel positions and starve relevant spans.

Representative findings from initial runs (summaries):
- 8k runs: mostly stable; truncation behavior predictable when chunk boundaries align with sentence boundaries. Minor bleed in aggressive prefetch with overlapping chunks (~1.6% PFR drop).
- 32k runs: increased incidence of sink events when retrieval returned 5+ overlapping chunks and prefetching merged chunks without re-ranker de-duplication. Observed attention mass concentrating on sentinel-like tokens inserted by older kd-prefetch module.
- 128k runs: several deterministic failures where delayed KV load (simulated 200–500ms per chunk) led to partial generation that later contradicts retrieved facts (KV cache mismatch index elevated). Some model variants showed graceful fallback; others produced coherent but incorrect summaries.

Failure case vignettes (investigation notes):
- VC-238: Chain retrieval returned doc A (offset 0–4k), doc B (4k–9k) with markers at join. The model ignored doc B's unique marker and repeated doc A content. Traces show attention head 11 focusing on token range in doc A after the boundary event. Hypothesis: kernel-level KV pointer arithmetic misapplies when contiguous chunk offsets exceed page size.
- VC-241: Prefetch dedupe failed to remove near-duplicates; overlapping spans resulted in repeated phrases being scored higher by the re-ranker and induced sink behavior. Short-term mitigation: enforce stricter Jaccard filter during prefetch.

Regression criteria and thresholds for onboarding gating:
- New model variant must meet PFR >= 0.95 on exact-copy probes at 8k, >= 0.92 at 32k, and >= 0.88 at 128k across the standard corpus.
- Sink event rate must be <0.5 per 1k requests at 32k and <2.5 per 1k requests at 128k for the default retrieval config.
- KV cache mismatch index must not increase by more than 10% relative to baseline for any sequence length.

Action items and remediation ideas:
- Instrumentation: add finer-grained KV cache sanity checks to the runtime to log chunk offsets and pointer arithmetic results when merging fetched chunks.
- Retrieval pipeline: implement overlapping-chunk canonicalization and sentinel-stripping during merge step; add a secondary re-ranker pass tuned for boundary continuity.
- Model prompts: include explicit boundary instructions in prompt templates during onboarding (e.g., "Do not assume continuation across split markers unless there is an explicit connector").
- CI integration: add five representative failure reproductions to the onboarding gate for model variants; fail the gate if any reproduce sink or PFR drops beyond thresholds.

Open questions and experiments to run next:
- Does quantized execution increase the incidence of pointer arithmetic bugs at the runtime level? (Schedule tests with Q4 quantized builds.)
- What is the interaction between attention-head freezing (low-rank adapters) and sink susceptibility? Run ablations with selective head masking.
- Are some re-ranker models more robust to near-duplicate overlapping spans? Benchmark three re-rankers on a curated overlap-heavy dataset.

Appendix (quick reproduction checklist):
1) Checkout model-evals/long-context-suite branch "chunk-boundary-probes".
2) Use corpus bundle "kb-long-2025-v2" and seed 42.
3) Run job: probes/boundary-bleed.yaml with lengths [8192,32768,131072].
4) Collect artifacts and attach the "retrieval.trace" file and head attention samples to the ticket.

Notes to reviewers: please try the boundary-confusion prompt with the new prefetch disabled and paste error traces in MLINF-904. This doc should be copied into the onboarding checklist once the CI jobs are added.
